evidence.quote: Starting next month, we will be purchasing $35 billion of securities per month, down $10 billion per month from our current rate.
the Committee anticipates that it likely will be appropriate to maintain the current target range for the federal funds rate, for a considerable time after the asset purchase program ends
I think recent readings on, for example, the CPI index have been a bit on the high side, but I think it’s—the data that we’re seeing is noisy.
Even given these declines, however, unemployment remains elevated, and a broader assessment of indicators suggests that underutilization in the labor market remains significant.
inflation continues to run well below our objective, and we're still some ways away from maximum employment. And for the moment, I don't see any tradeoff whatsoever in achieving our two objectives.
reaffirmed its view that a highly accommodative stance of monetary policy remains appropriate

parsed.rationale: The Committee continues its measured taper of asset purchases, which is mildly hawkish on the balance sheet, but keeps guidance of near-zero rates for a considerable time and of below-normal rates thereafter. The Chair dismisses higher inflation readings as noise and stresses that labor-market slack remains significant, giving a net dovish signal.
